variants.context: A composite benchmark evaluates several tasks or metrics under one declared protocol, then combines some of that evidence to support a bounded comparison or decision. variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Composite score
pairs.detail: Applies a normalization, weighting, and aggregation contract to produce one value or rank.
pairs.explanation: Applies a normalization, weighting, and aggregation contract to produce one value or rank. It is useful when a decision genuinely needs a scalar, but it embeds policy choices.

pairs.label: Evaluation dashboard
pairs.detail: Shows task, metric, subgroup, uncertainty, cost, and failure evidence without forcing all dimensions into one exchange rate.
pairs.explanation: Shows task, metric, subgroup, uncertainty, cost, and failure evidence without forcing all dimensions into one exchange rate. It is better for diagnosis and trade-off review.

variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Arithmetic mean
pairs.detail: Computes a weighted sum of normalized components.
pairs.explanation: Computes a weighted sum of normalized components. A strong result can offset a weak one, so use it only when that exchange is legitimate.

pairs.label: Geometric mean
pairs.detail: Multiplies positive normalized components through log space.
pairs.explanation: Multiplies positive normalized components through log space. A low component pulls the score down more strongly; zero and scaling policies must be explicit.

pairs.label: Worst case or hard floor
pairs.detail: Uses the weakest required component or checks every critical floor.
pairs.explanation: Uses the weakest required component or checks every critical floor. It protects must-pass capabilities but can create ties and noisy threshold behavior.
